To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mGlu5 metabotropic glutamate subtype is expressed in the early developing brain, but that its expression decreases with age.
the expression of the metabotopic glutamate receptor (mGluR)5 protein and mGluRs mRNA are developmentally regulated in a regionally specific fashion in the rat brain.
mGluR expression increases with development, and that this is due to a combination of post‐translational regulation and increased growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that glutamate plays in the developing brain.
the development of the glutamatergic system.
the expression and regulation of the mGluRs during brain development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a developmental increase in expression of mGluRs in the brain.

the developmental increase in the expression of the Group I metabotropic glutamate mGluR is due to both the increased amount of receptor protein present and the altered regional distribution of the receptor.

the expression of mGluRs in the developing brain is more complex than originally thought and that the expression of the mGluRs is not simply a function of receptor density, but also the expression of specific receptor subtypes, and that the expression and regulation of mGlu receptors may be regionally dependent and may differ between the two subfamilies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mGluR2 is expressed at high levels throughout development and that mGluRs are expressed at higher levels in the developing brain.
there is more mGlur5 protein and mRNA in developing brain than there is in adult brain.
mGluR expression changes during development, and that these changes may be due to a combination of increased growth of receptor poor regions and decreased expression in receptor rich regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are more mGluRs in the developing brain than in adults.

mGluR expression is enhanced in the early postnatal period in most brain regions, and that this is due in part to increased receptor expression in receptor‐poor brain areas and in part to increased expression in receptor‐rich brain areas.
the expression of mGluRs in developing brain is regulated in a manner different from the adult.
